    The radical filtration of ind(mod A) #

    The powers J^n of the categorical radical of ind(mod A) form a decreasing multiplicative filtration: J^{n+1} ⊆ J^n and J^m ∘ J^n ⊆ J^{m+n}. For a representation-finite algebra the radical is nilpotent: that paper argues that J consists of the matrix entries of the Jacobson radical of the endomorphism algebra of a finite additive generator. The formal nilpotence uses the nilpotence of the categorical radical of mod A, which is proved by that argument (LargeIndecomposable.Algebra.RightModuleRadical, nilpotentRadicalDataOfArtinianGenerator).

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
